review_basis: FD revision 2 plus Planner-accepted supplements communicated during this bounded design review; incorporate them into the FD before implementation.

findings.description: Browser CSP/CDP does not constrain Pandoc resource access for Markdown exports; offline and input-directory requirements need explicit coverage across backends.
findings.required_change: Use safe Go-generated self-contained HTML for Markdown exports and fixed Pandoc HTML reader; apply --sandbox, inspect ZIP XML resources and reject unsafe RST directives/remote images. Convert the checked snapshot only.

findings.description: ZIP versus wheel scope conflicts; authorization snapshot/digest rules and before-request redirect validation are unspecified.
findings.required_change: ZIP-only; SHA256 canonical parsed JSON snapshot using sorted compact ASCII JSON UTF8; strict platform and fields, reject redirects or validate every hop before request; reserve new target and copy exclusively, give explicit environment discovery guidance.

implementation_constraints: Configure CDP network blocking before Page.setDocumentContent; service asynchronous protocol events while awaiting responses.
Await Mermaid, fonts and all image decoding before print; reject script exceptions, failed resources and invalid PDF output.
Close Python temporary file handles before invoking Windows subprocesses; publish output without replacement.
Give HTML preprocessing and CDP transport clear subitem/interface boundaries without expanding approved scope.
Record accepted R1/R2 supplements in the FD before implementation; preserve ZIP executable permissions and verify entries before claiming installation success.
Failure during non-atomic directory copy must not report successful installation; clean only owned files or report a recovery path.
Do not download dependencies or run conversion tests under current authorization.
limitations: No runtime evidence for rendering quality, third-party integration, hand-written CDP/WebSocket or cross-platform browser behavior.
No execution of download, archive extraction, file publication or failure recovery paths.
An old FD-077 report path failed once; actual archive report path was then read successfully.
